title: Settings
desktopOnly: AI settings work in the desktop app. In the browser preview, open the page with ?mock=1 to try them with made-up data.

ai.noEncryption: Secure storage is not available on this computer, so keys cannot be saved.

busyLabels.reload: Asking the providers for their models

keySaved.one: Key saved, encrypted. It can use {count} chat model. Pick a model per role below, or ask for advice.
keySaved.other: Key saved, encrypted. It can use {count} chat models. Pick a model per role below, or ask for advice.

ai.adviceFrom: Advice from {model}: use it with [Use], try it with [Try], then [Save].
ai.noLongerOffered: No longer offered: the model for {roles}. Pick another.
ai.upToDate: Model lists are up to date; your chosen models are all still offered.
ai.connectFirst: Connect a key to choose models. Without a model, NPCs speak set lines and the chronicle comes from templates.

roles.chronicler: CHRONICLER (lore, requests and news, mostly at night)

ai.tryAdviceNote: plays the test set through the game with each, a few cents; the cheapest usable answer without leaks or false facts wins

budget.label: Budget per hour
budget.aria: Budget per hour of play in dollars
budget.adjusted: Saved as ${usd} an hour: a budget is at least ${least} and at most ${most}, against a slip of the keyboard.
budget.confirm: Are you sure? This lets the app spend up to ${usd} an hour.
budget.note: At 80% the chronicler and the goals of NPCs without a quest role wait; at 100% dialogue falls back to set lines.

spent.label: On your key
spent.today: today {usd} ({parts}). The game, the editor, a trial and a picture run count in the same budget.

replyWithin.label: Reply time
replyWithin.aria: How many seconds a spoken reply may take
replyWithin.adjusted: Saved as {seconds} seconds: a reply may take from {least} to {most} seconds.
replyWithin.note: How long the dialogue model may take for a reply, both tries together. Past it, the game's own line stands in. Large models need about ten.

askAbove.label: Ask first above
askAbove.aria: From what cost of one call the game asks first, in dollars
askAbove.saved: Saved: the game asks first before one call that costs more.
askAbove.adjusted: Saved as ${usd}: a cent at least, a thousand dollars at most.
askAbove.neverSaved: The game will not ask about cost; every call runs within the budgets.
askAbove.note: A call below this runs at once and shows in the status bar. Making a district or a region may cost more; then the game asks once.
askAbove.noteNever: The game never asks about cost. Set an amount to be asked again.

guide.label: Guide price
guide.hour: An hour of play as the guide counts it, with these models: about {hour}: {conversations} for 40 lines of talk, {goals} for 25 goal choices, {night} for the night's round.
guide.measured: An hour as it was measured, with goal choices, nights and journeys as they really come: about {usd}.
guide.lastHour: The last hour really cost {usd} on your key.
guide.place: A new place in a far town costs about {place} once, when you first do something there.
guide.parts: An hour of play with these models: {conversations} for 40 lines of talk, {goals} for 25 goal choices, {night} for the night's round.

pictures.title: PICTURES (places and people, optional)
pictures.about: Claude makes no pictures; the image models of OpenAI do. Each area (all its places share one picture) and each named person is drawn once, in the style of the world, and kept; generic people get a plain figure. At low quality a picture costs about half a cent to one cent (September 2026), and counts in the budget.
pictures.connectFirst: Connect an OpenAI key above to choose an image model.
pictures.noModels: no image models for this key
pictures.trialAlt: A trial picture of the start of the world
pictures.new: Make pictures of new places and people
pictures.newOn: What grows in play too: a far place, a district, a charted region, the people you meet there, in the style of the world or its land, when you come there or meet them. Counts in the budget.
pictures.newOff: Only the pictures there are (from the editor or from before); nothing new is drawn.

unpriced.one: The price of {model} ({role}) is not known: its tokens are counted, and it is called at most {count} time an hour ({callsThisHour} this hour).
unpriced.other: The price of {model} ({role}) is not known: its tokens are counted, and it is called at most {count} times an hour ({callsThisHour} this hour).

usage.input: {tokens} in ({percent} cached, {written} written to the cache)

credit.label: {name} credit
credit.stale: . Over 30 days old, please copy it again.
credit.note: Neither provider tells the game how much credit is left, so the game counts down from the balance you copy from their console. Other programs on the same account are not counted, hence "estimated".

usage.listPrices: Amounts are worked out from list prices. The invoice from the provider is what counts.

log.none: No model calls in the log yet.

display.keyboard: Everything can be done with the keyboard: type commands, Tab through the buttons, Escape closes a window. The story is read out by a screen reader as it comes. Nothing in the game needs quick reflexes: the clock stops while you type, in a fight, and in any window like this one.
display.rules: Show what does not come from the AI
display.rulesNote: Lines the game wrote itself (greetings, set lines, a line standing in for a slow or refused answer) get a warmer tint in the log and the talk window. Only while an AI model is chosen.
display.cardsNote: A place worth it the first time you reach it or see it rise from afar, and a tiding that changes things, come as a card over the log; the clock waits. Off, they are lines like any other.
display.soundNote: A quiet sound of where you are (wind in the reeds, the sea, a fire) and a bell on the hours it rings; the bell is a line in the text too, so nothing needs sound to be understood. Silent in menus and when the game waits.

transcript.on: Write a transcript of every game
transcript.how: Everything you see goes into a Markdown file: what you type, speech as quotes, the game's own lines in italics, a heading for each game day and each place. One file per game and per day, only ever added to; a large one goes on in a second file.

advanced.about: How the app itself behaves: saving, pausing, the AI log and how long a model may take. The rules of a world are its own knobs, in the editor.
advanced.desktopOnly: These work in the desktop app.
